topic: What happens if you lie in the sun?
title: What lying in the sun does
hook: What happens if you lie in the sun?

beats.label: 10 MINUTES
beats.line: Within minutes, sunlight on your skin starts making vitamin D.

beats.label: 15 MINUTES
beats.line: After fifteen minutes, UV rays can start damaging unprotected skin.

beats.label: 3 HOURS
beats.line: Three hours in, your skin can turn red, hot and sore.

beats.label: 3 DAYS
beats.line: By day three, a tan appears, but it only works like SPF three.

beats.label: 10 YEARS
beats.line: Ten years of sunbathing can show up as wrinkles and dark spots.

end.line: Do you tan, or do you burn?

description: From vitamin D to sunburn, tans and wrinkles: what lying in the sun does to your skin.

facts.claim: UVB light on bare skin turns 7-dehydrocholesterol into vitamin D3; about 5-30 minutes of sun a few times a week is often cited as enough.
facts.source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements (Vitamin D fact sheet)

facts.claim: Unprotected skin can be damaged by the sun's UV rays in as little as 15 minutes.
Sunburn signs (red, painful skin that is hot to the touch) usually appear within a few hours of too much sun.
Delayed tanning becomes visible about 2-3 days (48-72 h) after UV exposure; the extra melanin is a sign of damage and gives only about SPF 2 to 4.
facts.source: FDA (The Risks of Tanning) / PMC review on skin pigmentation (PMC8218595)

facts.claim: Repeated UV exposure causes photoaging (wrinkles, dark or age spots) and is considered the main cause of visible skin aging.
facts.source: American Academy of Dermatology / PMC review on UV photoaging (PMC12018068)
